question.text: This son of Henry the Fowler was crowned Holy Roman Emperor in 962. He defeated Magyar forces at Lechfeld.
question.clue: He had earlier thwarted Berengar, the king of Burgundy, by venturing into Italy a year before his coronation and marrying Adelaide, though he was drawn back to his homeland to put down a revolt by the Duke of Lotharingia, Conrad.

swap.leadin: Name some leaders associated with the 3rd Crusade.
swap.text: This German Holy Roman Emperor attempted to lead an army of 150,000 into the Holy Land, however, he drowned when his horse slipped while crossing the Saleph River.
swap.clue: He attempted to suppress the revolt of the Lombard League twice; the second time, the head of the Guelphs, Henry the Lion, refused to assist him.

question.text: After the Council of Constance, these wars were fought against Bohemians who followed the teachings of a namesake Czech reformer. Until his death, Jan Zizka led the radical Taborite faction to victories in these wars.
question.clue: Raids called "beautiful rides" were conducted by Prokop the Great in this conflict, which ended at the Battle of Lipany where the Utraquists defeated the Taborites.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the Thirty Years' War.
swap.text: The Bohemian period of the Thirty Years' War was ended by this 1620 battle near Prague, in which the Count of Tilly defeated Protestant forces lead by Christian of Anhalt.
swap.clue: Descartes may have been present at this one-hour battle, as an observer in the army of the count of Bucquoy.

question.text: Turgut Reis, a successor to this Muslim pirate, advised the Turks on how to capture the citadels during the siege. This corsair won the Battle of Preveza over the navy of Charles V and conquered Tunisia.
question.clue: Besides the pirate rulers of Algiers, Oruc and Hayreddin, another man with this epithet held a notable Diet at Besancon partially to legitimize his second marriage to Beatrice after his divorce from Adelheide.

swap.text: The attackers in the Battle of Wimpfen belonged to this organization that opposed the Protestant Union. A French organization founded by Henry, Duke of Guise was also named this two-word phrase.

question.leadin: FTPE, name some rulers of the Holy Roman Empire.
question.text: The first Emperor of the Saxon dynasty, this man resurrected the Empire from the ashes of the Carolingians after his victory at Lechfeld over the Magyars.
question.answerHtml: Otto I the Great (need one or the other)
question.clue: After further rebellions by his son Ludolph and by Conrad the Red, this man terminated their powers at the Imperial Diet of Auerstadt.

swap.leadin: Name these ruling families important in German history.
swap.text: From 1138 to 1208, this dynasty ruled over Germany, producing three Holy Roman Emperors, including Kaiser Friedrich Rotbart, better known as Frederick Barbarossa.
swap.clue: The decline of this dynasty was accompanied by the rise of the papacy-backed William of Holland, and saw the short rule of Conrad IV and the young Conradin.

question.text: Tilly's first defeat in the war was in this September 17, 1631 battle where Gustav Karlsson Horn executed one of the first troop shifts in modern warfare. Gustavus Adolphus's troops killed some 12,000 Imperial troops at this battle in Saxony.
question.clue: Another cavalry charge by Furstenberg drove off John George I and his Saxon troops, exposing the eventual victor's left flank.

swap.text: Holy Roman Emperor from 1152 to 1190, he supposedly sleeps atop Kyffhauser Mountain, waiting to save Germany. He lost a war with Pope Alexander III's Lombard League and led the Third Crusade.
swap.clue: This man was forced to sign the Treaty of Venice following his defeat at the Battle of Legnano by the Lombard League.

swap.text: Other key figures in the Thirty Years War included this general, whom Ferdinand II betrayed and replaced with Count Tilly.
swap.clue: This man's ardent opposition to the Edict of Restitution and his forced retreat at the Battle of Lutzen earned the ire of Ferdinand II, which culminated in the Holy Roman Emperor greenlighting his murder in 1634.

question.text: This 1629 decree of Ferdinand attempted to roll back the first decade of the Thirty Years War by restoring the Peace of Augsburg, infuriating Protestants who would have lost territory.
question.clue: Maximilian von Trautmannsdorf's Points of Pirna attempted to reconcile one party who had been alienated by this declaration, which was defended vociferously in Paul Laymann's Pacis Composito.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about the Thirty Years' War.
swap.text: The first stage of the war was a revolt, which began with this May 23, 1618 event in which Wilhelm Slavata and Jaroslav Borzita were thrown from a window and landed in a pile of manure.
swap.clue: Certain participants in this event claimed they had been saved by Churmusian angels, although they were probably saved by piles of horse manure.

question.leadin: The foremost early leader of this faction was Jacob of Mies, who preached at the University of Prague that the laity should receive the Eucharist in both bread and wine.
question.text: Name this moderate faction that maintained amicable relations with the Roman Catholic Church, and emerged victorious over their rivals at the Battle of Lipany during the Hussite Wars.
question.clue: The radical Taborites were opposed by this more moderate Hussite faction, who eventually broke with their brethren and fought on the side of the Catholics.

swap.text: Much of the Hussites' military success under Zizka stemmed from his pioneering of this tactic, in which bow and pistol-armed soldiers would hide in the namesake vehicles, and then charge once enemy cavalry faltered.
